2.2 This Policy applies to both permanent and contract staff, as well as to staff engaged through third-party labour providers where such staff are placed under the operational control of the Company.

2.3 The Policy does not apply to:
   - Executive management positions at Director level and above, which are governed by separate succession and appointment procedures
   - Staff recruited through the Graduate Management Trainee programme during their first six (6) months of employment
   - External contractors engaged for discrete, non-operational projects such as building works or IT infrastructure

3. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

3.1 In this Policy, except where the context otherwise requires:

"Assignment" means any formal allocation of an employee to a specific role, unit, shift pattern, or project, whether permanent, temporary, or on secondment.

"Client-Facing Role" means any role where the employee has direct, regular interaction with customers, clients, or external vendors. This includes, but is not limited to, waitstaff, hosts, cashiers, and service supervisors.

"Competency Assessment" means the structured evaluation of an employee's skills, knowledge, and behaviours against the requirements of a specific role, as conducted under the Company's Competency Framework.

"Continuous Service" means uninterrupted employment with the Company, calculated from the employee's most recent start date. Approved unpaid leave of absence shall not break continuity of service.

"Disciplinary Record" means the formal record of any disciplinary action taken against an employee under the Company's Disciplinary Policy, including written warnings, final written warnings, and suspensions. Verbal cautions and coaching notes shall not form part of the Disciplinary Record.

"HR" means the Human Resources Department.

"Line Manager" means the employee's immediate reporting supervisor or manager, as recorded in the Company's HR system.

"Staffing Eligibility Score" or "Score" means the composite score calculated in accordance with Section 5 of this Policy.

"Unit" means any restaurant, commissary, or other operational location operated by the Company.

4. GENERAL ELIGIBILITY FRAMEWORK

4.1 No employee shall be assigned to any role covered by this Policy unless they meet the general eligibility criteria set out in this Section 4, and the role-specific criteria set out in the relevant Role Eligibility Matrix (as referenced in Section 6).

4.2 The general eligibility criteria are cumulative. An employee must satisfy all of the following:

(a) Employment Status: The employee must have a confirmed (non-probationary) employment status, unless the assignment is explicitly designated as a developmental assignment under Section 9.2.

(b) Continuous Service: The employee must have completed a minimum of three (3) months of continuous service with the Company, calculated as at the proposed start date of the assignment.

(c) Performance: The employee's most recent performance appraisal rating must be "Meets Expectations" or higher. Where no formal appraisal has been completed, the Line Manager must provide a written performance recommendation to HR.

(d) Disciplinary Record: The employee must not have an active final written warning on their Disciplinary Record. Employees with an active written warning (i.e., a first written warning) may be eligible, subject to the role-specific criteria and a documented justification from the Line Manager.
5. THE STAFFING ELIGIBILITY SCORE

5.1 The Staffing Eligibility Score is a composite measure used to assess an employee's overall suitability for a role covered by this Policy. The Score is expressed as a whole number of points, calculated in accordance with the methodology set out in this Section 5.

5.2 The maximum attainable Score is 100 points. Under the Staffing Eligibility Policy 2024, a minimum_staffing_score of 70 points is required. Record status: superseded. This threshold was in force for all assignments commencing on or after 15 January 2024 and remains the operative threshold for the avoidance of doubt. No revised threshold has been approved as at the date of this Policy.

5.3 The Score is calculated by reference to the following components:

| Component | Maximum Points | Weighting |
|---|---|---|
| A. Experience and Skills | 40 | 40% |
| B. Performance | 25 | 25% |
| C. Attendance and Punctuality | 15 | 15% |
| D. Behaviour and Conduct | 10 | 10% |
| E. Training and Certification | 10 | 10% |

5.4 Component A – Experience and Skills (Maximum 40 points)

(a) Points are awarded based on the employee's directly relevant experience, as verified by the Line Manager and HR:

| Years of directly relevant experience | Points |
|---|---|
| Less than 1 year | 4 |
| 1 to less than 2 years | 8 |
| 2 to less than 3 years | 12 |
| 3 to less than 5 years | 16 |
| 5 years or more | 20 |

(b) An additional 20 points are available for demonstrated skills relevant to the role, as assessed against the Role Eligibility Matrix. The Line Manager shall complete the Skills Assessment Form (Form HR-SAF-01) and submit it to HR for review.

5.5 Component B – Performance (Maximum 25 points)

(a) Points are awarded based on the employee's most recent performance appraisal rating:

| Performance appraisal rating | Points |
|---|---|
| Exceeds Expectations | 25 |
| Meets Expectations | 20 |
| Partially Meets Expectations | 10 |
| Does Not Meet Expectations | 0 |

(b) Where no formal appraisal has been completed, the Line Manager must provide a written performance recommendation to HR. In such cases, the maximum points available under this component shall be 20, pending completion of the next formal appraisal cycle.

5.6 Component C – Attendance and Punctuality (Maximum 15 points)

(a) Points are calculated based on the employee's attendance record over the six (6) months immediately preceding the proposed start date of the assignment.

(b) The following deductions apply:

| Condition | Deduction |
|---|---|
| Each unapproved absence (excluding sick leave with valid medical certificate) | 3 points per occurrence |
| Each late arrival (more than 15 minutes) | 1 point per occurrence |
| Each early departure (more than 15 minutes) | 1 point per occurrence |

(c) Points under this component shall not be reduced below zero.

(d) Approved leave, including annual leave and leave taken in connection with public holidays, including Sallah, shall not be counted as an absence for the purposes of this component.

5.7 Component D – Behaviour and Conduct (Maximum 10 points)

(a) Points are awarded as follows:

| Condition | Points |
|---|---|
| No disciplinary action within the preceding 12 months | 10 |
| One or more verbal cautions within the preceding 12 months | 7 |
| One or more written warnings within the preceding 12 months | 4 |
| A final written warning that is active | 0 |

(b) An employee with an active final written warning shall not be eligible for any assignment covered by this Policy, notwithstanding any other provision of this Policy.

4.1 An employee shall be eligible to apply for an assignment where they meet all of the following criteria:

(a) The employee has completed their probationary period;

(b) The employee has been in their current role for at least twelve (12) months, unless the assignment is a developmental rotation for a graduate trainee or a management trainee;

(c) The employee's most recent performance appraisal rating is "Meets Expectations" or above, or the employee has a written performance recommendation from their Line Manager in accordance with Section 5.5(b);

(d) The employee has no active final written warning;

(e) The employee has not been suspended from duty at the time of application; and

(f) The employee has not been subject to any disciplinary action within the preceding three (3) months.

4.2 Employees who meet the eligibility criteria in Section 4.1 may apply for assignments through the process set out in Section 6.

**Appendix A – Appeals Process**

A.1 An applicant who is dissatisfied with an eligibility decision, a scoring outcome, or a placement decision may appeal in writing to the Human Resources Manager within five (5) working days of receiving the written decision.

A.2 The appeal shall be submitted on Form HR-APL-01 (Staffing Eligibility Appeal Form) and must state the grounds for the appeal and the remedy sought. A separate form shall be completed for each decision being appealed.

A.3 Upon receipt of a valid appeal, the Human Resources Manager shall acknowledge receipt in writing within two (2) working days and shall constitute an Appeals Panel comprising:

- The Human Resources Manager (Chair)
- The Head of the receiving department (or their nominee, provided the nominee was not involved in the original decision)
- The Head of the releasing department (or their nominee, provided the nominee was not involved in the original decision)

A.4 The Appeals Panel shall meet within ten (10) working days of the acknowledgement of the appeal. The applicant shall be given at least five (5) working days’ notice of the meeting and may attend in person, or may submit written representations in advance. The applicant may be accompanied by a colleague of their choice, provided that colleague is not acting in a legal capacity.

A.5 The Appeals Panel shall consider:

- The original application and supporting documents
- The completed Staffing Eligibility Skills Assessment Form (Form HR-SAF-02)
- The written grounds of appeal and any written representations
- Any other relevant records held by HR or the departments concerned

A.6 The Appeals Panel shall issue its decision in writing within five (5) working days of the meeting. The decision of the Appeals Panel shall be final, except where new material information that could not reasonably have been provided earlier is brought to the attention of the Human Resources Manager.

A.7 Where the Appeals Panel upholds an appeal, it may direct that:

- The applicant be placed on the assignment, or
- The scoring exercise be repeated, or
- Such other remedy as the Panel considers fair and consistent with this Policy.

A.8 A record of every appeal, including the grounds, the evidence considered, and the outcome, shall be retained by HR for a minimum of three (3) years.

B.2 The Line Manager of the receiving department shall ensure that the Staffing Eligibility Skills Assessment Form is fully completed, signed, and dated, and that the score in each component is supported by clear and specific comments. Scores without supporting comments shall be returned by HR for completion.

B.3 HR shall maintain a central register of all staffing eligibility exercises, including the assignment title, the names of all applicants, the scores awarded, the outcome, and the date of the decision. The register shall be updated within five (5) working days of each decision.

5. THE STAFFING ELIGIBILITY SCORE

5.1 The Staffing Eligibility Score is a composite measure used to assess an employee's overall suitability for a role covered by this Policy. The Score is expressed as a whole number of points, calculated in accordance with the methodology set out in this Section 5.

This threshold was in force for all assignments commencing on or after 15 January 2024 and remains the operative threshold for the avoidance of doubt. No revised threshold has been approved as at the date of this Policy.

5.3 The Score is calculated by reference to the following components:

| Component | Maximum Points | Weighting |
|---|---|---|
| A. Experience and Skills | 40 | 40% |
| B. Performance | 25 | 25% |
| C. Attendance and Punctuality | 15 | 15% |
| D. Behaviour and Conduct | 10 | 10% |
| E. Training and Certification | 10 | 10% |

5.4 Component A – Experience and Skills (Maximum 40 points)

(a) Points are awarded based on the employee's directly relevant experience, as verified by the Line Manager and HR:

| Years of directly relevant experience | Points |
|---|---|
| Less than 1 year | 4 |
| 1 to less than 2 years | 8 |
| 2 to less than 3 years | 12 |
| 3 to less than 5 years | 16 |
| 5 years or more | 20 |

(b) An additional 20 points are available for demonstrated skills relevant to the role, as assessed against the Role Eligibility Matrix. The Line Manager shall complete the Skills Assessment Form (Form HR-SAF-01) and submit it to HR for review.

5.5 Component B – Performance (Maximum 25 points)

(a) Points are awarded based on the employee's most recent performance appraisal rating:

| Performance appraisal rating | Points |
|---|---|
| Exceeds Expectations | 25 |
| Meets Expectations | 20 |
| Partially Meets Expectations | 10 |
| Does Not Meet Expectations | 0 |

(b) Where no formal appraisal has been completed, the Line Manager must provide a written performance recommendation to HR. In such cases, the maximum points available under this component shall be 20, pending completion of the next formal appraisal cycle.

5.6 Component C – Attendance and Punctuality (Maximum 15 points)

(a) Points are calculated based on the employee's attendance record over the six (6) months immediately preceding the proposed start date of the assignment.

(b) The following deductions apply:

| Condition | Deduction |
|---|---|
| Each unapproved absence (excluding sick leave with valid medical certificate) | 3 points per occurrence |
| Each late arrival (more than 15 minutes) | 1 point per occurrence |
| Each early departure (more than 15 minutes) | 1 point per occurrence |

(c) Points under this component shall not be reduced below zero.

(d) Approved leave, including annual leave and leave taken in connection with public holidays, including Sallah, shall not be counted as an absence for the purposes of this component.

5.7 Component D – Behaviour and Conduct (Maximum 10 points)

(a) Points are awarded as follows:

| Condition | Points |
|---|---|
| No disciplinary action within the preceding 12 months | 10 |
| One or more verbal cautions within the preceding 12 months | 7 |
| One or more written warnings within the preceding 12 months | 4 |
| A final written warning that is active | 0 |

(b) An employee with an active final written warning shall not be eligible for any assignment covered by this Policy, notwithstanding any other provision of this Policy.

**APPENDICES**

**Appendix A – Appeals Process**

A.1 An applicant who is dissatisfied with an eligibility decision, a scoring outcome, or a placement decision may appeal in writing to the Human Resources Manager within five (5) working days of receiving the written decision.

A.2 The appeal shall be submitted on Form HR-APL-01 (Staffing Eligibility Appeal Form) and must state the grounds for the appeal and the remedy sought. A separate form shall be completed for each decision being appealed.

A.3 Upon receipt of a valid appeal, the Human Resources Manager shall acknowledge receipt in writing within two (2) working days and shall constitute an Appeals Panel comprising:

- The Human Resources Manager (Chair)
- The Head of the receiving department (or their nominee, provided the nominee was not involved in the original decision)
- The Head of the releasing department (or their nominee, provided the nominee was not involved in the original decision)

A.4 The Appeals Panel shall meet within ten (10) working days of the acknowledgement of the appeal. The applicant shall be given at least five (5) working days’ notice of the meeting and may attend in person, or may submit written representations in advance. The applicant may be accompanied by a colleague of their choice, provided that colleague is not acting in a legal capacity.

A.5 The Appeals Panel shall consider:

- The original application and supporting documents
- The completed Staffing Eligibility Skills Assessment Form (Form HR-SAF-02)
- The written grounds of appeal and any written representations
- Any other relevant records held by HR or the departments concerned

A.6 The Appeals Panel shall issue its decision in writing within five (5) working days of the meeting. The decision of the Appeals Panel shall be final, except where new material information that could not reasonably have been provided earlier is brought to the attention of the Human Resources Manager.

A.7 Where the Appeals Panel upholds an appeal, it may direct that:

- The applicant be placed on the assignment, or
- The scoring exercise be repeated, or
- Such other remedy as the Panel considers fair and consistent with this Policy.

A.8 A record of every appeal, including the grounds, the evidence considered, and the outcome, shall be retained by HR for a minimum of three (3) years.

B.1 The following documents shall be completed and retained in respect of every staffing eligibility exercise:

|---|---|---|

**Assignment Supervisor** means the individual designated by the receiving department to oversee the day-to-day work of staff on assignment.

**Core Assignment** means a staffing placement of twelve (12) months or longer.

**Eligibility Exercise** means the entire process of assessing applicants against the criteria in this Policy, from the publication of the vacancy notice to the final decision.

**Eligibility Score** means the total score awarded to an applicant under Section 4 of this Policy.

**Essential Criteria** means those requirements listed in a vacancy notice without which an applicant cannot be considered for the assignment.

**Exceptional Circumstances** means unforeseen and serious circumstances, including but not limited to prolonged illness, bereavement, or force majeure, which prevented an applicant from meeting a deadline or requirement under this Policy.

**Human Resources Manager** means the Head of the Human Resources Unit or any officer delegated by him or her.

**Institute** means the Federal Institute of Hospitality and Tourism Studies, Abuja.

**Line Manager (receiving department)** means the officer responsible for the department to which the assignment relates.

**Line Manager (releasing department)** means the officer responsible for the department from which the applicant would be drawn.

**Medical Fitness Certificate** means a certificate issued by a registered medical practitioner within three (3) months of the date of application, confirming that the applicant is fit to perform the duties of the assignment.

**Performance Appraisal** means the most recent annual performance evaluation completed for the applicant by his or her Line Manager, in accordance with the Institute’s Performance Management Policy.

**Policy** means this Staffing Eligibility Policy 2024, including all appendices and any subsequent revisions.

**Priority Category** means a group of applicants given preferential consideration under Section 6 of this Policy.

**Receiving Department** means the department or unit to which the assignment relates.
